A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SICA/OpenMMSec research. The main text and Appendices A–E are readable, and equations, tables and retained figures can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original SICA evaluations on OpenMMSec, spectral and cross-domain analyses, ablations, and additional benchmark results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds post-processing robustness experiments and EigenCAM visualizations in Sections 5.6–5.7.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP backbone, low-rank attention updates, classification procedure and BCE objective remain unchanged. EigenCAM is introduced for analysis, without changing SICA's training or inference.

E1.justification: The datasets, four forensic domains and faking-type coverage are retained. Section 5.6 adds evaluation under Gaussian blur, Gaussian noise, JPEG compression and resizing, extending coverage to degraded input conditions.

E2.justification: The comparator memberships in the existing benchmark tables remain unchanged. The new robustness comparison in Figure 10 specifically evaluates Effort and TruFor against SICA, adding a comparison using these existing baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.6 introduces a randomly sampled, class-balanced subset of 2,500 real and 2,500 fake OpenMMSec images, evaluated using AUC across five settings per transformation. The existing training configuration, data splits and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially extends supplementary analysis with a four-condition robustness study and a separate EigenCAM interpretability study across all domains, including comparisons with tampering masks. The previous spectral analysis, cross-domain experiments, rank/backbone ablations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: There is no change in seed, repeated-run or statistical uncertainty reporting. The new robustness curves provide point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests, and the existing spectral-analysis reporting is retained.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged, including SICA's 85.4 average accuracy in Table 2. New Figure 10 shows SICA above Effort and TruFor throughout the displayed degradation settings; Figures 11–12 add qualitative findings about spatial focus.

T1.justification: The feature-space formulation, SVD definitions, projection operators and equations 1–8 remain mathematically unchanged. Renaming the heterogeneity phenomenon to the Ji-Zhe phenomenon introduces no new definition, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about artifact-space collapse, semantic structural priors, SICA, OpenMMSec and near-orthogonal reconstruction are retained. The phenomenon's new name and expanded benchmark description in the conclusion do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.7 interprets the new heatmaps as evidence of domain-specific artifact learning while acknowledging imperfect mask alignment. Appendix D.5 newly explains document class imbalance through source availability and privacy/copyright constraints, and asserts that it preserves evaluation validity. Existing semantic-backbone limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the code/data repository account from scu-zjz to venus-guangjian. v4 also identifies EigenCAM and its implementation reference, and acknowledges HYGON K100AI computational support. Appendix E.1's training details and Appendix A's release conditions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for the CAM library, Venus-DefakerOne, RITA and document-tampering research. Appendix C newly acknowledges proprietary closed-source unified detectors alongside ensembles. The main related-work organization and contribution positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits rename the phenomenon, refine the abstract and contributions, add Sections 5.6–5.7 and Appendix D.5, and update authorship, affiliations and acknowledgments. Most existing prose and section order remain intact. An unresolved COCO citation appears in Appendix D.3.3.

P2.justification: v4 adds the robustness plot and two attention-map figures, numbered 10–12. Existing figures are resized or relocated, and the former appendix Figures 10–11 become 13–14. The original visual content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new robustness tests and attention visualizations provide useful evidence that v2 lacked, while Appendix D.5 explains an existing dataset imbalance. The gains are limited: robustness sampling does not identify its source split or report repeated-run uncertainty, and the heatmaps and imbalance discussion do not establish their strongest assertions about interference and evaluation validity.
